title.zh: 卷23 列傳第15 蘇綽
title.raw: 卷23 列傳第15 蘇綽 Volume 23 Biographies 15: Su Chuo

sentences.zh: 蘇綽字令綽，武功人，魏侍中則之九世孫也。

translations.literal: Su Chuo, styled Lingchuo, was a man of Wugong, ninth-generation descendant of Wei Attendant-in-Chief Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo, styled Lingchuo, came from Wugong and was the ninth-generation descendant of Ze, Attendant-in-Chief of Wei.

sentences.zh: 累世二千石。

translations.literal: For generations his family held posts at the two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had held office at the two-thousand-bushel level.

sentences.zh: 父協，武功郡守。

translations.literal: His father Xie was administrator of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie served as administrator of Wugong commandery.

sentences.zh: 綽少好學，博覽羣書，尤善筭術。

translations.literal: Su Chuo from youth loved learning, broadly read many books, and was especially skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Su Chuo loved study, read widely, and was especially adept at reckoning and accounts.

sentences.zh: 從兄讓為汾州刺史，太祖餞于東都門外。

translations.literal: His older cousin Rang was governor of Fen Province; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai gave him a farewell feast outside the Eastern Capital Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When his older cousin Rang became governor of Fen Province, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw him off with a feast outside the Eastern Capital Gate.

sentences.zh: 臨別，謂讓曰：「卿家子弟之中，誰可任用者？

translations.literal: On parting, he said to Rang: "Among the young men of your house, who can be put to use?
translations.idiomatic: As they parted, he asked Rang: "Among the men of your clan, who is fit for service?

sentences.zh: 」讓因薦綽。

translations.literal: " Rang thereupon recommended Su Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang recommended Su Chuo.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃召為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then summoned him and made him palace aide of the mobile imperial secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned him and appointed him palace aide on the mobile imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 在官歲餘，太祖未深知之。

translations.literal: After more than a year in office, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai did not yet know him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo had been in office for more than a year before Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai truly knew his worth.

sentences.zh: 然諸曹疑事，皆詢於綽而後定。

translations.literal: Yet for doubtful matters in the various bureaus, all consulted Su Chuo before deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever a bureau faced a doubtful matter, it consulted Su Chuo before acting.

sentences.zh: 所行公文，綽又為之條式。

translations.literal: For official documents issued, Su Chuo also set up formulas for them.
translations.idiomatic: He also standardized the forms for all outgoing official documents.

sentences.zh: 臺中咸稱其能。

translations.literal: All within the secretariat praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the secretariat praised his competence.

sentences.zh: 後太祖與僕射周惠達論事，惠達不能對，請出外議之。

translations.literal: Later Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was discussing affairs with Vice Director Zhou Huida; Huida could not answer and asked to go out to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai debated policy with Vice Director Zhou Huida, Huida could not reply and asked leave to consult outside.

sentences.zh: 乃召綽，告以其事，綽即為量定。

translations.literal: He then summoned Su Chuo, told him the matter, and Su Chuo immediately weighed and decided it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned Su Chuo, explained the issue, and Su Chuo settled it at once.

sentences.zh: 惠達入呈，太祖稱善，謂惠達曰：「誰與卿為此議者？

translations.literal: Huida entered and presented it; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised it and said to Huida: "Who made this proposal with you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Huida returned and presented the answer, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai approved it and asked: "Who worked this out with you?"

sentences.zh: 」惠達以綽對，因稱其有王佐之才。

translations.literal: Huida answered with Su Chuo's name and thereby praised him as having talent to assist a king.
translations.idiomatic: Huida named Su Chuo and praised him as a man with the talent to assist a ruler.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「吾亦聞之久矣。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "I too have heard of this for a long time."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "I have heard the same for some time."

sentences.zh: 」尋除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo was soon appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 屬太祖與公卿往昆明池觀漁，行至城西漢故倉地，顧問左右，莫有知者。

translations.literal: It happened that Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai went with the high officials to Kunming Pool to watch fishing; when they reached the site of the Han-era granary west of the city, he looked back and asked those around him, but none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai went with the chief ministers to Kunming Pool to watch the fishing and passed the old Han granary west of the city, he turned and asked his attendants, but none knew what it was.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「蘇綽博物多通，請問之。

translations.literal: Someone said: "Su Chuo is widely learned and thoroughly informed—please ask him."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "Su Chuo knows everything—ask him."

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃召綽。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then summoned Su Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had Su Chuo summoned.

sentences.zh: 具以狀對。

translations.literal: He answered in full detail according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo answered in full, exactly as things were.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，因問天地造化之始，歷代興亡之迹。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was greatly pleased and thereupon asked about the beginning of heaven and earth's creation and transformation, and the traces of rise and fall through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was delighted and went on to ask about the origins of heaven and earth and the rise and fall of dynasties through history.

sentences.zh: 綽旣有口辯，應對如流。

translations.literal: Su Chuo being skilled in speech, he responded like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo was an eloquent speaker and answered without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 太祖益喜。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai grew even more pleased.

sentences.zh: 乃與綽並馬徐行至池，竟不設網罟而還。

translations.literal: He then rode side by side with Su Chuo at an easy pace to the pool; in the end they set no nets or weirs and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He rode beside Su Chuo at an easy pace to the pool, then turned back without ever casting a net.

sentences.zh: 遂留綽至夜，問以治道，太祖臥而聽之。

translations.literal: He kept Su Chuo until night and questioned him on the way of governance; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai lay down and listened.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Su Chuo until nightfall and questioned him on the art of governance while lying down to listen.

sentences.zh: 綽於是指陳帝王之道，兼述申韓之要。

translations.literal: Su Chuo thereupon pointed out and set forth the Way of emperors and kings, and together described the essentials of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo laid out the way of sage-kings and also expounded the core teachings of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃起，整衣危坐，不覺膝之前席。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then rose, straightened his garments and sat upright in awe, unconsciously advancing his knees past the mat's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sat up, straightened his robes, and listened with such rapt attention that he edged forward on his mat without noticing.

sentences.zh: 語遂達曙不厭。

translations.literal: The talk went on until dawn without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: They talked until dawn and still were not weary of it.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，謂周惠達曰：「蘇綽真奇士也，吾方任之以政。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, he said to Zhou Huida: "Su Chuo is truly an extraordinary man; I am about to entrust him with governance."
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he told Zhou Huida: "Su Chuo is a rare talent. I mean to put him in charge of government."

sentences.zh: 」即拜大行臺左丞，參典機密。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Left Assistant Director of the Grand Mobile Imperial Secretariat, participating in managing classified affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo was at once made Left Assistant Director of the Grand Mobile Imperial Secretariat and given a role in confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 自是寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: From then on favor and treatment grew daily loftier.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his favor and rank rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 綽始制文案程式，朱出墨入，及計帳、戶籍之法。

translations.literal: Su Chuo first devised document formulas—red outgoing, black incoming—and methods for account ledgers and household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo first established documentary procedures—red for outgoing papers, black for incoming ones—along with systems for fiscal accounts and household registers.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，齊神武三道入寇，諸將咸欲分兵禦之，獨綽意與太祖同。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Gao Huan entered in invasion on three routes; all the generals wanted to divide troops to resist, only Su Chuo's view matched Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, Gao Huan invaded on three fronts. The generals all wanted to split their forces to meet him, but only Su Chuo agreed with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 遂併力拒竇泰，擒之於潼關。

translations.literal: They thereupon combined strength to resist Dou Tai and captured him at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: They concentrated their strength against Dou Tai and captured him at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 四年，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫，封美陽縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was given the additional titles Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Viscount of Meiyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Viscount of Meiyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 加通直散騎常侍，進爵為伯，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Added Honest and Direct Regular Palace Attendant, advanced in rank to earl, fief increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title Honest and Direct Regular Palace Attendant, raised to earl, and granted two hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 十年，授大行臺度支尚書，領著作，兼司農卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Director of Revenue of the Grand Mobile Imperial Secretariat, concurrently heading the Palace Library, and also Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Director of Revenue of the Grand Mobile Imperial Secretariat, head of the Palace Library, and Minister of Agriculture as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖方欲革易時政，務弘彊國富民之道，故綽得盡其智能，贊成其事。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was just then wishing to reform current government and devoted himself to extending the way of strengthening the state and enriching the people, so Su Chuo was able to exhaust his intelligence and ability and assist in accomplishing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was then intent on reforming the government and strengthening the state and enriching the people, and Su Chuo was able to give his full talent to helping carry it out.

sentences.zh: 減官員，置二長，幷置屯田以資軍國。

translations.literal: He reduced official posts, established the two chiefs, and together established tuntian fields to supply army and state.
translations.idiomatic: He cut redundant offices, instituted the two-chief system, and set up tuntian colonies to support army and state.

sentences.zh: 又為六條詔書，奏施行之。

translations.literal: He also drafted the Six-Article Ordinances and memorialized to have them put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted the Six Ordinances and memorialized the throne to put them into effect.

sentences.zh: 其一，先治心，曰：

translations.literal: The first: first govern the heart, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The first ordinance, "First Govern the Heart," reads:

sentences.zh: 凡今之方伯守令，皆受命天朝，出臨下國，論其尊貴，並古之諸侯也。

translations.literal: All the regional overseers and magistrates of today receive mandate from the heavenly court, go out to oversee subordinate states; speaking of their honor and eminence, they all are like the feudal lords of old.
translations.idiomatic: All the regional governors and magistrates of today receive their commissions from the imperial court and go out to govern the lands below; in rank and dignity they are the equals of the feudal lords of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 是以前世帝王，每稱共治天下者，唯良宰守耳。

translations.literal: Therefore past emperors and kings, whenever they spoke of jointly ruling all under Heaven, meant only good magistrates and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the emperors and kings of former ages, when they spoke of ruling the realm together with others, meant nothing more than good local administrators.

sentences.zh: 明知百僚卿尹，雖各有所司，然其治民之本，莫若宰守之最重也。

translations.literal: Clearly knowing that the hundred officials and commandery chiefs, though each has his charge, yet the root of governing the people—nothing is weightier than magistrates and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: It is well known that though the hundred officials and commandery chiefs each have his own duties, the foundation of governing the people lies above all with magistrates and prefects.

sentences.zh: 凡治民之體，先當治心。

translations.literal: In general the substance of governing the people—one must first govern the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The first principle of governing the people is to govern the heart.

sentences.zh: 心者，一身之主，百行之本。

translations.literal: The heart is the master of one's person, the root of the hundred conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The heart is the ruler of the body and the root of every act.

sentences.zh: 心不清淨，則思慮妄生。

translations.literal: If the heart is not clear and pure, then thoughts and considerations arise wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: When the heart is not clear, wayward thoughts arise.

sentences.zh: 思慮妄生，則見理不明。

translations.literal: If thoughts arise wrongly, then seeing principle is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: When wayward thoughts arise, one cannot see principle clearly.

sentences.zh: 見理不明，則是非謬亂。

translations.literal: If seeing principle is not clear, then right and wrong are confused and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: When principle is not seen clearly, right and wrong fall into confusion.

sentences.zh: 是非謬亂，則一身不能自治，安能治民也！

translations.literal: If right and wrong are confused, then one person cannot govern himself—how can he govern the people!
translations.idiomatic: When right and wrong are confused, a man cannot even govern himself—how can he govern others!

sentences.zh: 是以治民之要，在清心而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the essential of governing the people lies in clearing the heart, that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the key to governing the people is to purify the heart.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂清心者，非不貪貨財之謂也，乃欲使心氣清和，志意端靜。

translations.literal: What is called clearing the heart is not the meaning of not coveting goods and wealth—it is wishing to make heart-and-breath clear and harmonious, will and intent upright and still.
translations.idiomatic: Purifying the heart does not mean merely refusing to grasp for wealth; it means keeping the spirit clear and calm and the will upright and steady.

sentences.zh: 心和志靜，則邪僻之慮，無因而作。

translations.literal: When heart is harmonious and will still, then perverse and crooked considerations have no occasion by which to arise.
translations.idiomatic: When the heart is calm and the will settled, crooked impulses find no opening.

sentences.zh: 邪僻不作，則凡所思念，無不皆得至公之理。

translations.literal: When perversity does not arise, then whatever one thinks and considers—none fails to attain the principle of utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When crooked impulses do not arise, every thought naturally tends toward perfect fairness.

sentences.zh: 率至公之理以臨其民，則彼下民孰不從化。

translations.literal: Leading with the principle of utmost fairness to oversee one's people, then which of those common people below would not follow and be transformed?
translations.idiomatic: Rule the people with perfect fairness, and who among them will not submit and be transformed?

sentences.zh: 是以稱治民之本，先在治心。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said the root of governing the people lies first in governing the heart.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the foundation of governing the people begins with governing the heart.

sentences.zh: 其次又在治身。

translations.literal: Second, moreover, is governing the body.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes governing oneself.

sentences.zh: 凡人君之身者，乃百姓之表，一國之的也。

translations.literal: Every ruler's person is the model for the hundred surnames, the target of the whole state.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's own person is the standard for the people and the mark at which the whole realm aims.

sentences.zh: 表不正，不可求直影；

translations.literal: If the model is not straight, one cannot seek a straight shadow;
translations.idiomatic: If the standard is crooked, you cannot expect a straight shadow;

sentences.zh: 的不明，不可責射中。

translations.literal: If the target is not clear, one cannot blame for not hitting the shot.
translations.idiomatic: if the mark is unclear, you cannot demand a bull's-eye.

sentences.zh: 今君身不能自治，而望治百姓，是猶曲表而求直影也；

translations.literal: Now if the ruler's person cannot govern itself yet one hopes to govern the hundred surnames—it is like a crooked model yet seeking a straight shadow;
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler cannot govern himself yet expects to govern the people, it is like setting up a crooked standard and hoping for a straight shadow;

sentences.zh: 君行不能自脩，而欲百姓脩行者，是猶無的而責射中也。

translations.literal: If the ruler's conduct cannot cultivate itself yet one wishes the hundred surnames to cultivate conduct—it is like having no target yet blaming for not hitting the shot.
translations.idiomatic: if he cannot discipline his own conduct yet demands disciplined conduct from the people, it is like shooting at no mark and then blaming the archer for missing.

sentences.zh: 故為人君者，必心如清水，形如白玉。

translations.literal: Therefore one who is ruler must have heart like clear water, form like white jade.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must keep a heart as clear as water and a bearing as pure as white jade.

sentences.zh: 躬行仁義，躬行孝悌，躬行忠信，躬行禮讓，躬行廉平，躬行儉約，然後繼之以無倦，加之以明察。

translations.literal: Personally practice benevolence and righteousness, personally practice filial piety and brotherly duty, personally practice loyalty and trust, personally practice rites and yielding, personally practice integrity and fairness, personally practice frugality and economy—then continue with unwearying effort, add to it scrutiny and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He must himself practice benevolence and righteousness, filial piety and brotherly duty, loyalty and trustworthiness, rites and forbearance, integrity and fairness, and thrift—then press on without tiring and add clear-sighted judgment.

sentences.zh: 行此八者，以訓其民。

translations.literal: Practicing these eight things, to instruct one's people.
translations.idiomatic: By living out these eight virtues he teaches his people.

sentences.zh: 是以其人畏而愛之，則而象之，不待家教日見而自興行矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the people fear and love him, take him as model and emulate him—without waiting for household instruction, day by day they see and by themselves rise up in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Then the people will revere and love him, take him as their model, and day by day practice virtue of their own accord without waiting to be taught at home.

sentences.zh: 其二，敦教化，曰：

translations.literal: The second: encourage teaching and transformation, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The second ordinance, "Encourage Teaching and Transformation," reads:

sentences.zh: 天地之性，唯人為貴。

translations.literal: The nature of heaven and earth—only the human is honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the nature of heaven and earth, humanity alone is held supreme.

sentences.zh: 明其有中和之心，仁恕之行，異于木石，不同禽獸，故貴之耳。

translations.literal: Clearly knowing they have the heart of centered harmony and conduct of benevolence and forbearance, different from wood and stone, not the same as birds and beasts—therefore they are honored.
translations.idiomatic: Humans possess a heart of balanced harmony and a capacity for benevolence and forbearance; unlike wood and stone, unlike birds and beasts—that is why they are honored.

sentences.zh: 然性無常守，隨化而遷。

translations.literal: Yet nature has no constant holding—it shifts according to transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet human nature has no fixed form; it changes with the influences around it.

sentences.zh: 化于敦朴者，則質直；

translations.literal: Transformed by solid simplicity, then substance is straight;
translations.idiomatic: Shaped by plain sincerity, people become honest and upright;

sentences.zh: 化於澆偽者，則浮薄。

translations.literal: Transformed by thin deceit, then floating and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: shaped by shallow artifice, they become frivolous and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 浮薄者，則衰弊之風；

translations.literal: The floating and shallow—that is the wind of decay and decline;
translations.idiomatic: Frivolity and corruption produce a climate of decline;

sentences.zh: 質直者，則淳和之俗。

translations.literal: The straight in substance—that is the custom of pure harmony.
translations.idiomatic: honesty and uprightness produce a custom of simple goodness.

sentences.zh: 衰弊則禍亂交興，淳和則天下自治。

translations.literal: Decay and decline then disaster and disorder arise in succession; pure harmony then all under Heaven governs itself.
translations.idiomatic: Where decline spreads, calamity and rebellion follow one after another; where simple goodness prevails, the realm orders itself.

sentences.zh: 治亂興亡，無不皆由所化也。

translations.literal: Order and disorder, rise and fall—none fail to all come from what transforms them.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a age knows order or chaos, prosperity or ruin, all comes from the forces that shape it.

sentences.zh: 然世道雕喪，已數百年。

translations.literal: Yet the way of the age has withered and decayed—for hundreds of years already.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the moral order of the age has been wasting away for centuries.

sentences.zh: 大亂滋甚，且二十歲。

translations.literal: Great disorder has grown extreme, for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Great chaos has grown worse for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 民不見德，唯兵革是聞；

translations.literal: The people do not see virtue—only arms and warfare they hear;
translations.idiomatic: The people have seen no virtue—only the sound of arms;

sentences.zh: 上無教化，惟刑罰是用。

translations.literal: Above there is no teaching and transformation—only punishments are used.
translations.idiomatic: above them there has been no moral instruction—only punishment.

sentences.zh: 而中興始爾，大難未平，加之以師旅，因之以饑饉，凡百草創，率多權宜。

translations.literal: Yet restoration has only just begun, great hardship is not yet settled—added to this are armies on campaign, compounded by famine; for all hundred things newly created, mostly there are expedients.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration has only just begun, great dangers are not yet past, armies are still on campaign, and famine follows in their wake. In rebuilding everything from the ground up, most measures have had to be makeshift.

sentences.zh: 致使禮讓弗興，風俗未改。

translations.literal: This causes rites and yielding not to rise, customs not yet changed.
translations.idiomatic: That is why rites and forbearance have not taken root and old habits remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 比年稍登稔，徭賦差輕，衣食不切，則教化可脩矣。

translations.literal: In recent years harvests have slightly prospered, corvée and tax are somewhat lighter, clothing and food not pressing—then teaching and transformation can be cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years harvests have improved somewhat, levies have eased, and people are no longer desperate for food and clothing—now moral instruction can be restored.

sentences.zh: 凡諸牧守令長，宜洗心革意，上承朝旨，下宣教化矣。

translations.literal: All overseers, prefects, and magistrates ought to wash the heart and renew intent, above receiving court directives, below spreading teaching and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Every governor, prefect, and magistrate should cleanse his heart and change his ways—carry out the court's orders above and spread moral instruction below.

sentences.zh: 夫化者，貴能扇之以淳風，浸之乙太和，被之以道德，示之以朴素。

translations.literal: As for transformation—it prizes being able to fan it with pure wind, steep it in the Great Harmony, cover it with morality and virtue, show it simplicity and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: True transformation means stirring people with wholesome custom, soaking them in harmony, clothing them in moral example, and showing them simplicity.

sentences.zh: 使百姓亹亹，中遷於善，邪偽之心，嗜欲之性，潛以消化，而不知其所以然，此之謂化也。

translations.literal: Make the hundred surnames diligent and earnest, midway shift toward good—the heart of perversity and falsehood, the nature of craving and desire—covertly digested and dissolved without knowing why it is so; this is called transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Let the people advance steadily toward goodness until crooked impulses and greedy desires quietly melt away without their even knowing why—that is transformation.

sentences.zh: 然後教之以孝悌，使民慈愛；

translations.literal: Then teach them filial piety and brotherly duty, make the people loving and kind;
translations.idiomatic: Then teach filial piety and brotherly duty so that the people become loving and tender;

sentences.zh: 教之以仁順，使民和睦；

translations.literal: Teach them benevolence and obedience, make the people harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: teach benevolence and gentleness so that they live in harmony;

sentences.zh: 教之以禮義，使民敬讓。

translations.literal: Teach them rites and righteousness, make the people reverent and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: teach rites and righteousness so that they become respectful and forbearing.

sentences.zh: 慈愛則不遺其親，和睦則無怨於人，敬讓則不競於物。

translations.literal: Loving kindness then does not abandon one's kin, harmony then bears no resentment toward others, reverence and yielding then do not compete over things.
translations.idiomatic: Where love prevails, no one forsakes his family; where harmony prevails, no one bears grudges; where respect and forbearance prevail, no one quarrels over possessions.

sentences.zh: 三者旣備，則王道成矣。

translations.literal: When the three are all complete, then the kingly Way is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When these three are fully in place, the kingly Way is achieved.

sentences.zh: 此之謂教也。

translations.literal: This is called teaching.
translations.idiomatic: That is what is meant by teaching.

sentences.zh: 先王之所以移風易俗，還淳反素，垂拱而治天下以至太平者，莫不由此。

translations.literal: The reason the former kings could shift winds and change customs, return to purity and revert to plainness, fold hands in sleeve and govern all under Heaven until reaching great peace—none fail to come from this.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the ancient kings could change customs, restore simplicity, and rule the realm in effortless peace was none other than this.

sentences.zh: 此之謂要道也。

translations.literal: This is called the essential Way.
translations.idiomatic: That is the essential path.

sentences.zh: 其三，盡地利，曰：

translations.literal: The third: exhaust the land's advantage, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The third ordinance, "Make Full Use of the Land," reads:

sentences.zh: 人生天地之間，以衣食為命。

translations.literal: Human life between heaven and earth—take clothing and food as fate.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings live between heaven and earth on clothing and food alone.

sentences.zh: 食不足則饑，衣不足則寒。

translations.literal: If food is insufficient then hunger; if clothing insufficient then cold.
translations.idiomatic: Without enough food they go hungry; without enough clothing they go cold.

sentences.zh: 饑寒切體，而欲使民興行禮讓者，此猶逆阪走丸，勢不可得也。

translations.literal: Hunger and cold cutting the body, yet wishing to make the people rise up and practice rites and yielding—this is like rolling a ball uphill against the slope; by its momentum it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger and cold gnaw at the body, to expect the people to practice rites and forbearance is like rolling a ball uphill—it cannot be done by force of will alone.

sentences.zh: 是以古之聖王，知其若此，故先足其衣食，然後教化隨之。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of old, knowing that matters are like this, first made the people's clothing and food sufficient, and only then followed with teaching and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old knew this, and so they first saw that the people had enough food and clothing before they turned to moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 夫衣食所以足者，在於地利盡。

translations.literal: For clothing and food to be sufficient lies in fully using the land's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Food and clothing become sufficient only when the land's potential is fully used.

sentences.zh: 地利所以盡者，由於勸課有方。

translations.literal: For the land's advantage to be fully used is due to having proper methods of urging and supervising cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: The land is fully used only when cultivation is urged and supervised by sound methods.

sentences.zh: 主此教者，在乎牧守令長而已。

translations.literal: Those who preside over this instruction are simply the overseers, prefects, and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Those responsible for this work are simply the governors, prefects, and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 民者冥也，智不自周，必待勸教，然後盡其力。

translations.literal: The people are dim; their intelligence does not reach everywhere by itself—they must await urging and instruction before they can exert their full strength.
translations.idiomatic: The common people are inert; left to themselves they cannot see what to do—they need guidance and instruction before they will give their full effort.

sentences.zh: 諸州郡縣，每至歲首，必戒敕部民，無問少長，但能操持農器者，皆令就田，墾發以時，勿失其所。

translations.literal: In all provinces, commanderies, and counties, at the start of each year one must charge and command the people under one's jurisdiction: regardless of age, all who can handle farming tools are to be sent to the fields, opening land at the proper season without missing the time.
translations.idiomatic: In every province, commandery, and county, at the year's opening each official must charge his people: young or old, anyone who can wield a farm tool is to go to the fields, breaking ground in season and missing no proper time.

sentences.zh: 及布種旣訖，嘉苗須理，麥秋在野，蠶停於室，若此之時，皆宜少長悉力，男女併功，若援溺、救火、寇盜之將至，然後可使農夫不廢其業，蠶婦得就其功。

translations.literal: When sowing has finished, fine seedlings need tending; at wheat harvest they are in the fields, silkworms stop work in the rooms—at times like these all young and old should exert full strength, men and women work together, as if rescuing the drowning, fighting fire, or bandits about to arrive; only then can farmers not abandon their work and silk women complete their labor.
translations.idiomatic: When sowing is done, seedlings need tending; at wheat harvest people belong in the fields, and when silkworms rest in the rooms everyone, young and old, men and women together, must labor as if saving the drowning, fighting a fire, or repelling bandits—only then will farmers keep at their work and silk workers finish theirs.

sentences.zh: 若有遊手怠惰，早歸晚出，好逸惡勞，不勤事業者，則正長牒名郡縣，守令隨事加罰，罪一勸百。

translations.literal: If there are idlers who are lazy, returning early and going out late, loving ease and hating toil, not diligently pursuing their livelihood—then the neighborhood heads register their names and report to the commandery and county, and overseers and magistrates impose punishment according to circumstances; punishing one warns a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone idles, leaves early, comes back late, loves ease and hates labor, and neglects his livelihood, the neighborhood heads should register his name and report him to the commandery and county, and the governor or magistrate should punish him as the case requires—one punishment to warn a hundred.

sentences.zh: 此則明宰之教也。

translations.literal: This is the instruction of a wise administrator.
translations.idiomatic: That is how a capable administrator teaches.

sentences.zh: 夫百畝之田，必春耕之，夏種之，秋收之，然後冬食之。

translations.literal: For a hundred-mu field one must plow in spring, sow in summer, and harvest in autumn—only then eat in winter.
translations.idiomatic: A field of a hundred mu must be plowed in spring, sown in summer, and harvested in autumn before it can feed anyone in winter.

sentences.zh: 此三時者，農之要也。

translations.literal: These three seasons are the essentials of farming.
translations.idiomatic: These three seasons are the heart of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 若失其一時，則穀不可得而食。

translations.literal: If one season is missed, then grain cannot be obtained for eating.
translations.idiomatic: Miss one of them and there will be no grain to eat.

sentences.zh: 故先王之戒曰：「一夫不耕，天下必有受其饑者；

translations.literal: Therefore the warning of the former kings says: "If one man does not plow, under Heaven there will surely be someone who suffers hunger from it;
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ancient kings warned: "If one man does not plow, someone under Heaven will go hungry because of it;

sentences.zh: 一婦不織，天下必有受其寒者。

translations.literal: If one woman does not weave, under Heaven there will surely be someone who suffers cold from it.
translations.idiomatic: if one woman does not weave, someone under Heaven will go cold because of it.

sentences.zh: 」若此三時不務省事，而令民廢農者，是則絕民之命，驅以就死然。

translations.literal: " If at these three seasons one does not attend to lightening affairs and causes the people to abandon farming—it is cutting off the people's life and driving them toward death.
translations.idiomatic: " If at these three seasons officials do not simplify their duties and instead make the people neglect farming, they cut off the people's livelihood and drive them toward death.

sentences.zh: 單劣之戶，及無牛之家，勸令有無相通，使得兼濟。

translations.literal: For weak and poor households and families without cattle, urge that those who have and those who lack may exchange and aid each other, enabling mutual relief.
translations.idiomatic: For weak, poor households and families without oxen, urge those who have resources and those who lack them to help one another so that all may be sustained.

sentences.zh: 三農之隙，及陰雨之暇，又當教民種桑、植果，藝其菜蔬，脩其園圃，畜育雞豚，以備生生之資，以供養老之具。

translations.literal: In the intervals between the three farm seasons and during rainy-day leisure, one should also teach the people to plant mulberry, set out fruit trees, cultivate vegetables, keep up gardens, raise chickens and pigs, to provide for daily sustenance and supply what is needed in old age.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals between the three farming seasons and on rainy days when fieldwork stops, teach the people to plant mulberry, set out fruit trees, grow vegetables, tend gardens, and raise chickens and pigs, so they have daily sustenance and something to live on in old age.

sentences.zh: 夫為政不欲過碎，碎則民煩；

translations.literal: In governing one should not wish to be excessively detailed—detailed then the people are troubled;
translations.idiomatic: In governing, one should not be excessively fussy—too much detail wears the people down;

sentences.zh: 勸課亦不容太簡，簡則民怠。

translations.literal: Urging cultivation also cannot permit excessive simplicity—simple then the people grow slack.
translations.idiomatic: yet urging cultivation cannot be too lax either—too lax and the people grow idle.

sentences.zh: 善為政者，必消息時宜而適煩簡之中。

translations.literal: One who governs well must assess and balance the timely needs and hit the mean between trouble and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: A good administrator must weigh the season's needs and strike the right balance between burden and ease.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：「不剛不柔，布政優優，百祿是求。

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes says: "Neither hard nor soft, spread governance at ease, seek the hundred blessings.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Odes says: "Neither hard nor soft, spread rule with ease, and seek the hundred blessings.

sentences.zh: 」如不能爾，則必陷於刑辟矣。

translations.literal: " If one cannot be like this, then one must fall into criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: " Fail at that, and one is sure to fall under the penal code.

sentences.zh: 其四，擢賢良，曰：

translations.literal: The fourth: promote the worthy and good, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The fourth ordinance, "Promote the Worthy and Good," reads:

sentences.zh: 天生蒸民，不能自治，故必立君以治之。

translations.literal: Heaven produces the teeming people—they cannot govern themselves, therefore a ruler must be set up to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven produces the multitudes of people, but they cannot govern themselves; therefore a ruler must be established to govern them.

sentences.zh: 人君不能獨治，故必置臣以佐之。

translations.literal: The ruler cannot govern alone, therefore ministers must be set up to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler cannot govern alone, and so ministers must be appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 上至帝王，下及郡國，置臣得賢則治，失賢則亂，此乃自然之理，百王不能易也。

translations.literal: From emperors and kings above down to commanderies and states below—if ministers appointed are worthy then there is order, if unworthy then disorder; this is the natural principle, which no king through the ages can change.
translations.idiomatic: From emperors and kings down to commanderies and counties, appoint worthy ministers and there is order; appoint unworthy ones and there is chaos. That is nature's law, and no dynasty has ever changed it.

sentences.zh: 今刺史守令，悉有僚吏，皆佐治之人也。

translations.literal: Today's inspectors, overseers, and magistrates all have staff officers—they are all people who assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Today's inspectors, governors, and magistrates all have subordinate officials, and every one of them helps govern.

sentences.zh: 刺史府官則命於天朝，其州吏以下，並牧守自置。

translations.literal: Inspectors' bureau officials are appointed by the heavenly court; all state officials below them are appointed by the overseers themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An inspector's secretariat staff are appointed by the imperial court, but all other provincial officials are chosen by the governor himself.

sentences.zh: 自昔以來，州郡大吏，但取門資，多不擇賢良；

translations.literal: From old times, for major posts in provinces and commanderies they took only family pedigree, mostly not selecting the worthy and good;
translations.idiomatic: From of old, major provincial and commandery posts have gone by family pedigree, with little regard for worth;

sentences.zh: 末曹小吏，唯試刀筆，並不問志行。

translations.literal: For petty bureau clerks they tested only brush and knife, and did not ask about intent and conduct at all.
translations.idiomatic: petty clerks have been chosen by brush-and-knife tests alone, with no inquiry into character.

sentences.zh: 夫門資者，乃先世之爵祿，無妨子孫之愚瞽；

translations.literal: Family pedigree is the rank and emolument of former generations—it does not prevent stupid blindness in descendants;
translations.idiomatic: Family pedigree is inherited rank and salary from past generations—it does not keep a descendant from being dull or blind;

sentences.zh: 刀筆者，乃身外之末材，不廢性行之澆偽。

translations.literal: Brush and knife are external minor talents—they do not eliminate falsity and baseness in one's nature and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: brush-and-knife skill is an outward, minor talent—it does not rule out deceit and corruption of character.

sentences.zh: 若門資之中而得賢良，是則策騏驥而取千里也；

translations.literal: If among family pedigree one obtains the worthy and good, that is like spurring a qiji and taking a thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: If pedigree yields a worthy man, it is like spurring a thousand-li steed;

sentences.zh: 若門資之中而得愚瞽，是則土牛木馬，形似而用非，不可以涉道也。

translations.literal: If among family pedigree one obtains stupid blindness, that is like an earthen ox or wooden horse—similar in form but useless in function, and cannot be used to travel the Way.
translations.idiomatic: if pedigree yields a fool, it is like an earthen ox or wooden horse—shaped like the real thing but useless on the road.

sentences.zh: 若刀筆之中而得志行，是則金相玉質，內外俱美，實為人寶也；

translations.literal: If among brush and knife one obtains intent and conduct, that is like gold appearance and jade substance, beautiful inside and out—truly a treasure among men;
translations.idiomatic: If clerical skill is joined to good character, it is gold outside and jade within—a true treasure among men;

sentences.zh: 若刀筆之中而得澆偽，是則飾畫朽木，悅目一時，不可以充榱椽之用也。

translations.literal: If among brush and knife one obtains baseness and falsity, that is like painting rotten wood—pleasing to the eye for a moment, but cannot be used to fill rafters and beams.
translations.idiomatic: if clerical skill hides baseness and deceit, it is painted rotten wood—pleasing for a moment but unfit to bear a roof beam.

sentences.zh: 今之選舉者，當不限資蔭，唯在得人。

translations.literal: Today's selectors ought not to be limited by pedigree and inherited privilege—what matters is obtaining the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Selection today should not be bound by pedigree and inherited privilege; what matters is getting the right man.

sentences.zh: 苟得其人，自可起塚養而為卿相，伊尹、傅說是也，而況州郡之職乎。

translations.literal: If one obtains the right man, one can raise him from tending graves and rearing cattle to minister and chancellor—Yi Yin and Fu Yue were such; how much more for provincial and commandery posts!
translations.idiomatic: Get the right man and he may rise from tending graves and feeding cattle to minister and chancellor, as with Yi Yin and Fu Yue—how much more so for provincial office!

sentences.zh: 苟非其人，則丹朱、商均雖帝王之胤，不能守百里之封，而況於公卿之冑乎。

translations.literal: If he is not the right man, then Dan Zhu and Shang Jun, though heirs of emperors and kings, could not keep a fief of a hundred li—how much less the descendants of high ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Get the wrong man and even Dan Zhu and Shang Jun, though sons of kings, could not hold a hundred-li fief—much less the offspring of great ministers.

sentences.zh: 由此而言，觀人之道可見矣。

translations.literal: From this speaking, the Way of observing men can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: From this the way to judge men becomes clear.

sentences.zh: 凡所求材藝者，為其可以治民。

translations.literal: All talent and skill that is sought is because it can govern the people.
translations.idiomatic: Talent and skill are sought because they can be used to govern the people.

sentences.zh: 若有材藝而以正直為本者，必以其材而為治也；

translations.literal: If there is talent and skill with uprightness as the root, one will surely use that talent for governance;
translations.idiomatic: If a man has talent but takes uprightness as his root, that talent will be turned to good government;

sentences.zh: 若有材藝而以姦偽為本者，將由其官而為亂也，何治之可得乎。

translations.literal: If there is talent and skill with treachery and falsity as the root, disorder will come through his office—how can governance be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: if he has talent but takes treachery and deceit as his root, his office will breed disorder—what governance can come of that?

sentences.zh: 是故將求材藝，必先擇志行。

translations.literal: Therefore in seeking talent and skill, one must first select intent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, in seeking talent, character must come first.

sentences.zh: 其志行善者，則舉之；

translations.literal: Those whose intent and conduct are good—promote them;
translations.idiomatic: Promote those whose character is good;

sentences.zh: 其志行不善者，則去之。

translations.literal: Those whose intent and conduct are not good—remove them.
translations.idiomatic: remove those whose character is bad.

sentences.zh: 而今擇人者多云「邦國無賢，莫知所舉」。

translations.literal: Yet today those who select men often say: "The state has no worthies—I do not know whom to promote."
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who choose officials today often say, "There are no worthy men in the realm—I do not know whom to promote."

sentences.zh: 此乃未之思也，非適理之論。

translations.literal: This is failure to think it through—not a statement fitting reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is thoughtlessness, not sound reasoning.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，古人有言：明主聿興，不降佐於昊天；

translations.literal: The reason is this—the ancients had a saying: when a bright lord rises, he does not descend to seek assistants from vast Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: when a wise ruler rises, he does not look to Heaven for assistants;

sentences.zh: 大人基命，不擢才於后土。

translations.literal: When a great man receives mandate, he does not pluck talent from the broad earth.
translations.idiomatic: when a great man receives the mandate, he does not pluck talent from the earth below.

sentences.zh: 常引一世之人，治一世之務。

translations.literal: He always leads the men of one age to govern the affairs of one age.
translations.idiomatic: He always leads the men of his own age to govern the affairs of his own age.

sentences.zh: 故殷、周不待稷、契之臣，魏、晉無假蕭、曹之佐。

translations.literal: Therefore Yin and Zhou did not wait for ministers like Ji and Qi; Wei and Jin had no need to borrow assistants like Xiao and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Yin and Zhou did not wait for men like Hou Ji and Qi; Wei and Jin did not have to borrow aides like Xiao He and Cao Shen.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「十室之邑，必有忠信如丘者焉。

translations.literal: Zhongni said: "In a settlement of ten households, there must be someone as loyal and trustworthy as Qiu."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "In a hamlet of ten households there must be someone as loyal and trustworthy as I am."

sentences.zh: 」豈有萬家之都，而云無士，但求之不勤，擇之不審，或用之不得其所，任之不盡其材，故云無耳。

translations.literal: " How can there be a city of ten thousand households and yet say there are no scholars—it is only that one does not seek diligently, does not select carefully, or employs them not in the right place, assigns them not according to their talent, and therefore says there are none.
translations.idiomatic: " How can a city of ten thousand households have no talent? People say there are none only because they do not search diligently, choose carefully, appoint men to the right posts, or use their abilities fully.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「千人之秀曰英，萬人之英曰雋。

translations.literal: The ancients said: "A thousand men's excellence is called ying; ten thousand men's ying is called jun."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Outstanding among a thousand is called ying; outstanding among ten thousand is called jun."

sentences.zh: 」今之智效一官，行聞一邦者，豈非近英雋之士也。

translations.literal: " Today's men whose wisdom suffices for one office and whose conduct is heard in one state—are they not nearly men of ying and jun?
translations.idiomatic: " Are not the men today whose ability fits one office and whose reputation fills one province nearly such outstanding figures?

sentences.zh: 但能勤而審察，去虛取實，各得州郡之最而用之，則民無多少，皆足治矣。

translations.literal: If one can be diligent and examine carefully, discard the empty and take the solid, and employ each according to the best fit in provinces and commanderies, then whether the people are many or few, all can be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Search diligently, examine carefully, discard the hollow and keep the real, and appoint each man to the post in province or commandery that suits him best, and people will be governable whether they are many or few.

sentences.zh: 孰云無賢！

translations.literal: Who says there are no worthies!
translations.idiomatic: Who can say there are no worthy men!

sentences.zh: 夫良玉未剖，與瓦石相類；

translations.literal: Fine jade uncut is like tile and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Uncut fine jade looks like ordinary tile and stone;

sentences.zh: 名驥未馳，與駑馬相雜。

translations.literal: A famous thoroughbred unrun mixes with nags.
translations.idiomatic: an unridden famous steed is indistinguishable from a nag.

sentences.zh: 及其剖而瑩之，馳而試之，玉石駑驥，然後始分。

translations.literal: When it is cut and polished, run and tested—then jade and stone, nag and thoroughbred, for the first time are distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Cut and polish the jade, run and test the horse—only then do jade and stone, thoroughbred and nag, stand apart.

sentences.zh: 彼賢士之未用也，混於凡品，竟何以異。

translations.literal: When worthy scholars are not yet employed, they mix with ordinary ranks—how in the end are they different?
translations.idiomatic: Before worthy men are employed, they mingle with the common run—how can anyone tell the difference?

sentences.zh: 要任之以事業，責之以成務，方與彼庸流較然不同。

translations.literal: The essential is to entrust them with real tasks and hold them responsible for completed duties—only then are they clearly different from those mediocre streams.
translations.idiomatic: The point is to give them real work and hold them accountable for results—only then do they stand clearly apart from the mediocre crowd.

sentences.zh: 昔呂望之屠釣，百里奚之飯牛，甯生之扣角，管夷吾之三敗，當此之時，悠悠之徒，豈謂其賢。

translations.literal: In old times Lü Wang butchered and fished, Baili Xi fed cattle, Ning Sheng beat horns, and Guan Yiwu was thrice defeated—at that time the drifting masses, how could they have called them worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Once Lü Wang was a butcher and fisherman, Baili Xi fed cattle, Ning Sheng played horn, and Guan Yiwu was defeated three times—at the time, who among ordinary men would have called them worthy?

sentences.zh: 及升王朝，登霸國，積數十年，功成事立，始識其奇士也。

translations.literal: When they ascended the royal court and entered hegemonic states, accumulated decades, achievement completed and affairs established—only then did they recognize them as extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered the royal court and rose in hegemonic states, and after decades of achievement people finally recognized them as extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 於是後世稱之，不容於口。

translations.literal: Thereupon later ages praised them—could not contain it in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Then later ages praised them without end.

sentences.zh: 彼瑰偉之材，不世之傑，尚不能以未遇之時，自異於凡品，況降此者哉。

translations.literal: Those magnificent talents, unworldly heroes—even they could not, in times when they had not yet met opportunity, distinguish themselves from ordinary ranks; how much less those below them!
translations.idiomatic: Even such magnificent, once-in-an-age talents could not, before their chance came, distinguish themselves from ordinary men—how much less lesser men!

sentences.zh: 若必待太公而後用，是千載無太公；

translations.literal: If one must wait for Grand Duke before employing anyone, then for a thousand years there would be no Grand Duke;
translations.idiomatic: If you must wait for a Taigong before appointing anyone, there will be no Taigong for a thousand years;

sentences.zh: 必待夷吾而後任，是百世無夷吾。

translations.literal: If one must wait for Yiwu before assigning anyone, then for a hundred generations there would be no Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: if you must wait for a Guan Yiwu before assigning anyone, there will be no Guan Yiwu for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，士必從微而至著，功必積小以至大，豈有未任而已成，不用而先達也。

translations.literal: The reason is this—a scholar must go from obscurity to prominence, achievement must accumulate from small to great; how could there be achievement already complete before office is held, or advancement before employment?
translations.idiomatic: Talent rises from obscurity to fame, and achievement grows from small to great—how can there be finished achievement before office, or advancement before use?

sentences.zh: 若識此理，則賢可求，士可擇。

translations.literal: If one recognizes this principle, then worthies can be sought and scholars can be selected.
translations.idiomatic: Understand this, and worthy men can be found and talent can be chosen.

sentences.zh: 得賢而任之，得士而使之，則天下之治，何向而不可成也。

translations.literal: Obtain worthies and assign them, obtain scholars and employ them—then governing all under Heaven, what direction could not be accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: Find worthy men and appoint them, find talent and use it, and there is no direction in which good government cannot be achieved.

sentences.zh: 然善官人者必先省其官。

translations.literal: Yet one who is good at assigning men must first reduce the number of offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a ruler who knows how to appoint men must first reduce the number of offices.

sentences.zh: 官省，則善人易充，善人易充，則事無不理；

translations.literal: When offices are few, good men are easy to fill; when good men are easy to fill, then nothing in affairs fails to be ordered;
translations.idiomatic: Fewer offices make it easier to fill them with good men; when good men are easy to find, affairs fall naturally into order;

sentences.zh: 官煩，則必雜不善之人，雜不善之人，則政必有得失。

translations.literal: When offices are numerous, then unworthy men must be mixed in; when unworthy men are mixed in, then in governance there must be gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: too many offices force unworthy men into service, and when unworthy men are mixed in, government inevitably goes wrong.

sentences.zh: 故語曰：「官省則事省，事省則民清；

translations.literal: Therefore a saying goes: "Few offices then few affairs; few affairs then the people are clear;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Few offices mean few affairs; few affairs mean a clear-minded people;

sentences.zh: 官煩則事煩，事煩則民濁。

translations.literal: Numerous offices then numerous affairs; numerous affairs then the people are turbid.
translations.idiomatic: numerous offices mean numerous affairs; numerous affairs mean a confused people.

sentences.zh: 」清濁之由，在於官之煩省。

translations.literal: " Whether clear or turbid—the cause lies in whether offices are numerous or few.
translations.idiomatic: " Clarity or confusion among the people depends on whether offices are many or few.

sentences.zh: 案今吏員，其數不少。

translations.literal: Examining today's official posts, their number is not small.
translations.idiomatic: Look at the official roster today and the number is not small.

sentences.zh: 昔民殷事廣，尚能克濟，況今戶口減耗，依員而置，猶以為少。

translations.literal: Formerly when the people were numerous and affairs broad, they could still manage; how much more now when household registers have declined—setting posts by quota, they still think it too few.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when the population was larger and business more extensive, the state still managed; now, with fewer households, officials are kept at full quota and still deemed too few.

sentences.zh: 如聞在下州郡，尚有兼假，擾亂細民，甚為無理。

translations.literal: As I have heard, in lower provinces and commanderies there are still concurrent acting appointments, disturbing the common people—very unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in lower provinces and commanderies men still hold concurrent acting appointments, harassing ordinary people—a gross abuse.

sentences.zh: 諸如此輩，悉宜罷黜，無得習常。

translations.literal: All such as these ought entirely to be dismissed and removed—do not let old habit continue.
translations.idiomatic: All such cases should be dismissed and abolished; old habit must not be allowed to stand.

sentences.zh: 非直州郡之官，宜須善人，爰至黨族閭裏正長之職，皆當審擇，各得一鄉之選，以相監統。

translations.literal: Not only provincial and commandery officials need good men—even down to clan heads, neighborhood heads, and village chiefs, all ought to be carefully selected, each obtaining the best choice of one village, to supervise and oversee together.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only provincial and commandery officials who must be good men—even clan heads, neighborhood heads, and village chiefs should be carefully chosen, each the best man of his community, to supervise and keep watch together.

sentences.zh: 夫正長者，治民之基。

translations.literal: Neighborhood heads are the foundation of governing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Neighborhood heads are the foundation of governing the people.

sentences.zh: 基不傾者，上必安。

translations.literal: If the foundation does not tilt, above must be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If the foundation does not shift, the structure above stands firm.

sentences.zh: 凡求賢之路，自非一途。

translations.literal: All paths of seeking worthies are not of one route alone.
translations.idiomatic: There is more than one path to finding worthy men.

sentences.zh: 然所以得之審者，必由任而試之，考而察之。

translations.literal: Yet the reason one can obtain them with certainty is that one must necessarily test them through assignment, examine and inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: But the way to know you have the right man is to appoint him, test him, examine him, and inspect him.

sentences.zh: 起于居家，至於鄉黨，訪其所以，觀其所由，則人道明矣，賢與不肖別矣。

translations.literal: Starting from home life, reaching to village and neighborhood—inquire into his motives, observe his course; then the Way among men is clear, and worthy and unworthy are distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From his conduct at home to his reputation in village and neighborhood, inquire into his motives and observe his ways—then human character becomes clear and the worthy stand apart from the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 率此以求，則庶無愆悔矣。

translations.literal: Following this to seek, then mostly there will be no fault or regret.
translations.idiomatic: Search in this way and you will rarely err or regret your choice.

sentences.zh: 其五，恤獄訟，曰：

translations.literal: The fifth: care for prisons and litigation, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The fifth ordinance, "Care for Prisons and Litigation," reads:

sentences.zh: 人受陰陽之氣以生，有情有性。

translations.literal: Human beings receive yin and yang qi to be born—they have feeling and have nature.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings are born from the qi of yin and yang; they have both feeling and nature.

sentences.zh: 性則為善，情則為惡。

translations.literal: Nature is what is good; feeling is what is evil.
translations.idiomatic: Nature tends toward good; feeling tends toward evil.

sentences.zh: 善惡旣分，而賞罰隨焉。

translations.literal: Once good and evil are divided, reward and punishment follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once good and evil are distinguished, reward and punishment follow.

sentences.zh: 賞罰得中，則惡止而善勸；

translations.literal: When reward and punishment hit the mean, evil stops and good is encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: When rewards and punishments are balanced, evil ceases and good is encouraged;

sentences.zh: 賞罰不中，則民無所措手足。

translations.literal: When reward and punishment do not hit the mean, the people have nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: when they are not balanced, the people do not know where to put hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 民無所措手足，則怨叛之心生。

translations.literal: When the people have nowhere to set hand or foot, then the heart of resentment and rebellion is born.
translations.idiomatic: When the people do not know where to stand, resentment and rebellion arise.

sentences.zh: 是以先王重之，特加戒慎。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings weighted this heavily and added special caution and care.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ancient kings treated this matter with special weight and caution.

sentences.zh: 夫戒慎者，欲使治獄之官，精心悉意，推究事源。

translations.literal: What is called caution and care is wishing to make officials who govern prisons concentrate the heart and exhaust intent, and push investigation to the source of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Caution means requiring prison officials to concentrate their minds, investigate thoroughly, and trace each case to its source.

sentences.zh: 先之以五聽，參之以證驗，妙睹情狀，窮鑒隱伏，使姦無所容，罪人必得。

translations.literal: First use the five modes of hearing, cross-check with evidence and verification, subtly perceive the state of feeling, exhaustively discern what is hidden—so that treachery has nowhere to hide and the guilty must be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Begin with the five modes of hearing, cross-check with evidence, read the emotions subtly, and penetrate what is hidden, so that deceit has no refuge and the guilty are surely found.

sentences.zh: 然後隨事加刑，輕重皆當，赦過矜愚，得情勿喜。

translations.literal: Then according to the matter impose punishment—light and heavy all appropriate; pardon transgressions and pity the foolish; when the facts are obtained do not rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Then punish according to the case, with penalties neither too light nor too heavy; pardon faults and show mercy to the simple-minded; and when the truth is found, do not exult.

sentences.zh: 又能消息情理，斟酌禮律，無不曲盡人心，遠明大教，使獲罪者如歸。

translations.literal: Also able to balance reason and sentiment, weigh rites and law, in every case fully understanding the human heart, making the great teaching clear from afar, making those who receive punishment feel as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: They could also weigh reason against sentiment and rites against law, fully grasp the human heart, make the great moral teaching clear, and leave the punished feeling as though they had come home.

sentences.zh: 此則善之上也。

translations.literal: This is the highest goodness.
translations.idiomatic: That is the highest standard.

sentences.zh: 然宰守非一，不可人人皆有通識，推理求情，時或難盡。

translations.literal: Yet overseers and magistrates are not one person; not everyone can have thorough insight; reasoning to seek sentiment sometimes cannot be fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: But overseers and magistrates are many, and not every man can see all the way through a case by reasoning alone.

sentences.zh: 唯當率至公之心，去阿枉之志，務求曲直，念盡平當。

translations.literal: One should only lead with utmost fairness, remove partial and wrong intent, strive to ascertain right and wrong, and keep perfect equity in mind.
translations.idiomatic: They should only act from utmost fairness, put aside favor and distortion, seek the truth of each case, and aim at perfect equity.

sentences.zh: 聽察之理，必窮所見，然後栲訊以法，不苛不暴，有疑則從輕，未審不妄罰，隨事斷理，獄無停滯。

translations.literal: In hearing and investigating cases, one must exhaust what is seen, then examine by law, neither harsh nor violent; when in doubt lean toward leniency, do not punish rashly when not yet verified; decide cases as matters arise, prisons without backlog.
translations.idiomatic: In hearing cases they must pursue every lead, then examine by law without harshness or violence; where doubt remains, lean toward leniency; where guilt is unproved, do not punish; decide each matter promptly so that prisons never stall.

sentences.zh: 此亦其次。

translations.literal: This is next in rank.
translations.idiomatic: That is the middle standard.

sentences.zh: 若乃不仁恕而肆其殘暴，同民木石，專任捶楚。

translations.literal: If one is not benevolent and forgiving but indulges cruelty and violence, treats the people like wood and stone, and relies solely on beating and torture—
translations.idiomatic: But if a man is not humane or forgiving and indulges cruelty, treating people like wood and stone and relying only on beatings and torture—

sentences.zh: 巧詐者雖事彰而獲免，辭弱者乃無罪而被罰。

translations.literal: the cunning and deceitful though their crime is clear escape punishment, while the weak in speech though innocent are punished.
translations.idiomatic: the cunning escape though their guilt is plain, while the inarticulate innocent are punished.

sentences.zh: 有如此者，斯則下矣，非共治所寄。

translations.literal: Those who are like this are the lowest grade—not what good governance relies on.
translations.idiomatic: Such men belong to the lowest grade and are unfit to share in governing.

sentences.zh: 今之宰守，當勤於中科，而慕其上善。

translations.literal: Today's overseers and magistrates should diligently aim for the middle grade and aspire to the highest goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Today's overseers and magistrates should strive for the middle standard and aim at the highest.

sentences.zh: 如在下條，則刑所不赦。

translations.literal: If like the lowest category, the law will not pardon.
translations.idiomatic: If they fall to the lowest grade, the law will not spare them.

sentences.zh: 又當深思遠大，念存德教。

translations.literal: They should also think deeply and far-sightedly, keeping moral instruction in mind.
translations.idiomatic: They should also think deeply and keep moral instruction in view.

sentences.zh: 先王之制曰，與殺無辜，寧赦有罪；

translations.literal: The former kings' regulation said: rather than kill the innocent, better to pardon the guilty;
translations.idiomatic: The ancient rule said: better to pardon the guilty than to kill the innocent;

sentences.zh: 與其害善，寧其利淫。

translations.literal: rather than harm the good, better to let the wicked benefit.
translations.idiomatic: better to let the wicked go free than to harm the good.

sentences.zh: 明必不得中，寧濫舍有罪，不謬害善人也。

translations.literal: Clearly if one cannot hit the mark, better to loose the guilty in excess than wrongly harm good people.
translations.idiomatic: If the mark cannot be hit, it is better to release too many guilty men than to wrong a single good one.

sentences.zh: 今之從政者則不然。

translations.literal: Those in government today are not like this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who govern today do the opposite.

sentences.zh: 深文巧劾，甯致善人于法，不免有罪于刑。

translations.literal: They stretch the law with cunning accusations, rather bring good people under the law than fail to punish the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: They twist the law with clever accusations, preferring to ensnare the innocent rather than let the guilty escape.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，皆非好殺人也，但云為吏寧酷，可免後患。

translations.literal: The reason is none love killing, but they say that as an official better be harsh, and later trouble can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is not that they love killing, but that they say a harsh official avoids future trouble.

sentences.zh: 此則情存自便，不念至公，奉法如此，皆姦人也。

translations.literal: This is keeping convenience in mind, not thinking of utmost fairness; serving the law thus—all are wicked people.
translations.idiomatic: That is self-interest, not fairness; men who serve the law in this way are wicked.

sentences.zh: 夫人者，天地之貴物，一死不可複生。

translations.literal: Human beings are the precious things of heaven and earth; once dead they cannot live again.
translations.idiomatic: Man is heaven and earth's most precious creature; once dead, he cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 然楚毒之下，以痛自誣，不被申理，遂陷刑戮者，將恐往往而有。

translations.literal: Yet under torture, confessing falsely from pain, not given fair hearing, thus falling into punishment and death—this probably happens often.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under torture men falsely confess from pain, receive no fair hearing, and are sent to their deaths—this surely happens all too often.

sentences.zh: 是以自古以來，設五聽三宥之法，著明慎庶獄之典，此皆愛民甚也。

translations.literal: Therefore since antiquity the five hearings and three pardons have been instituted, and clear classics of careful handling of cases established—all show great love for the people.
translations.idiomatic: That is why antiquity established the five hearings and three pardons and set forth careful rules for judging cases—all signs of deep love for the people.

sentences.zh: 凡伐木殺草，田獵不順，尚違時令，而虧帝道；

translations.literal: Even cutting wood, killing grass, and hunting out of season still violate seasonal rules and harm the imperial Way;
translations.idiomatic: Even felling trees, cutting grass, or hunting out of season violates the seasons and mars the imperial Way;

sentences.zh: 況刑罰不中，濫害善人，甯不傷天心、犯和氣也！

translations.literal: how much more when punishments miss the mark and good people are harmed—would this not wound heaven's heart and violate harmonious qi!
translations.idiomatic: how much more when punishments miss the mark and good people are harmed—does that not wound heaven's heart and violate the harmonious qi!

sentences.zh: 天心傷，和氣損，而欲陰陽調適，四時順序，萬物阜安，蒼生悅樂者，不可得也。

translations.literal: When heaven's heart is wounded and harmonious qi harmed, to want yin and yang balanced, the four seasons in order, all things flourishing, and the people happy—cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven's heart is wounded and harmonious qi is lost, how can yin and yang stay balanced, the seasons keep order, all things flourish, and the people live in joy?

sentences.zh: 故語曰，一夫籲嗟，王道為之傾覆，正謂此也。

translations.literal: Hence the saying: one man's sigh can overturn the kingly Way—just this is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: one man's sigh can overturn the kingly Way—this is what it means.

sentences.zh: 凡百宰守，可無慎乎。

translations.literal: All hundred overseers and magistrates—can they not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Should not every overseer and magistrate take heed?

sentences.zh: 若有深姦巨猾，傷化敗俗，悖亂人倫，不忠不孝，故為背道者，殺一利百，以清王化，重刑可也。

translations.literal: If there are deep wickedness and great scoundrels who harm transformation, ruin customs, rebel against human relations, are unfilial and disloyal, and deliberately go against the Way—kill one to benefit a hundred, to clear kingly transformation; heavy punishment is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: But where deep villainy and great scoundrels harm moral order, ruin custom, overturn human relations, and deliberately rebel against the Way, to kill one and benefit a hundred, clearing the kingly transformation, heavy punishment is justified.

sentences.zh: 識此二途，則刑政盡矣。

translations.literal: Knowing these two paths, then legal administration is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Once these two paths are understood, penal administration is complete.

sentences.zh: 其六，均賦役，曰：

translations.literal: The sixth: equalize levies and corvée, it says:
translations.idiomatic: The sixth ordinance, "Equalize Levies and Corvée," reads:

sentences.zh: 聖人之大寶曰位。

translations.literal: The sage's great treasure is called the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's greatest treasure is the throne.

sentences.zh: 何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財。

translations.literal: What guards the throne? Benevolence. What gathers people? Wealth.
translations.idiomatic: What guards the throne is benevolence; what gathers people is wealth.

sentences.zh: 明先王必以財聚人，以仁守位。

translations.literal: Clearly the former kings must use wealth to gather people and use benevolence to guard the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the ancient kings used wealth to gather people and benevolence to keep the throne.

sentences.zh: 國而無財，位不可守。

translations.literal: A state without wealth—the throne cannot be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Without wealth a state cannot keep its throne.

sentences.zh: 是故

translations.literal: Therefore
translations.idiomatic: Therefore

translations.literal: (Three Five).
translations.idiomatic: [Since the Three Five]

sentences.zh: 三以來，皆有徵稅之法。

translations.literal: since then, all have had methods of taxation.
translations.idiomatic: since then, every age has had systems of taxation.

sentences.zh: 雖輕重不同，而濟用一也。

translations.literal: Though light and heavy differ, the purpose of supplying needs is one.
translations.idiomatic: Though the burdens differ in weight, the purpose of meeting public needs is the same.

sentences.zh: 今逆寇未平，軍用資廣，雖未遑減省，以恤民瘼，然令平均，使下無匱。

translations.literal: Today the rebel enemy is not yet pacified and military expenses are vast; though there is not yet leisure to reduce and economize to relieve the people's distress, still order equal distribution so that those below are not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Today the rebels are not yet subdued and military costs are heavy; though we cannot yet cut levies to ease the people's distress, we must still distribute burdens evenly so that none below are ruined.

sentences.zh: 夫平均者，不舍豪強而征貧弱，不縱姦巧而困愚拙，此之謂均也。

translations.literal: Equal distribution means not sparing the powerful and strong while taxing the poor and weak, and not indulging the cunning while burdening the simple and dull—this is called equal.
translations.idiomatic: Equal distribution means not exempting the powerful while taxing the weak, nor favoring the cunning while crushing the simple—that is what equality means.

sentences.zh: 故聖人曰：「蓋均無貧。」

translations.literal: Therefore the sage said: "When all is equal, none are poor."
translations.idiomatic: As the sage said: "When all is equal, none are poor."

sentences.zh: 然財貨之生，其功不易。

translations.literal: Yet the production of wealth and goods is not easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wealth is not easily produced.

sentences.zh: 織紝紡績，起於有漸，非旬日之間，所可造次。

translations.literal: Weaving and spinning begin gradually and cannot be hurried in a matter of days.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving and spinning build up by degrees and cannot be produced in a few days.

sentences.zh: 必須勸課，使預營理。

translations.literal: One must encourage and supervise, making people prepare in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials must encourage and supervise people so that they prepare in advance.

sentences.zh: 絹鄉先事織紝，麻土早脩紡績。

translations.literal: In silk districts let weaving come first; in hemp districts let spinning be readied early.
translations.idiomatic: In silk districts let weaving begin early; in hemp districts let spinning be prepared ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 先時而備，至時而輸，故王賦獲供，下民無困。

translations.literal: Prepared beforehand and delivered on time, thus the royal levies are supplied and the people below are not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Prepared in advance and delivered on time, the royal levies are met and the people are not distressed.

sentences.zh: 如其不預勸戒，臨時迫切，複恐稽緩，以為己過，捶扑交至，取辦目前。

translations.literal: If there is no advance encouragement and warning, and at the deadline urgency presses, again fearing delay and taking it as one's own fault, beatings come one after another to get results at once.
translations.idiomatic: Without advance warning, officials panic at the deadline, fear delay as their own fault, and resort to beatings to force immediate payment.

sentences.zh: 富商大賈，緣茲射利，有者從之貴買，無者與之舉息。

translations.literal: Great merchants and traders, seizing this chance for profit, sell dear to those who have money and lend at interest to those who have none.
translations.idiomatic: Great merchants seize the chance for profit, selling dear to those with money and lending at interest to those without.

sentences.zh: 輸稅之民，於是弊矣。

translations.literal: The people who pay taxes are thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The tax-paying people are ruined by it.

sentences.zh: 租稅之時，雖有大式，至於斟酌貧富，差次先後，皆事起於正長，而系之於守令。

translations.literal: At the time of rent and tax, though there is a great standard, as for weighing rich and poor and ordering precedence, all matters begin with the headmen and depend on the magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: At tax time, though a general rule exists, adjusting for rich and poor and setting the order of payment all begin with the headmen and rest with the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 若斟酌得所，則政和而民悅；

translations.literal: If the weighing is appropriate, then government is harmonious and the people are pleased;
translations.idiomatic: If the adjustment is fair, government is harmonious and the people are content;

sentences.zh: 若檢理無方，則吏姦而民怨。

translations.literal: if investigation and management are without method, then clerks are wicked and the people resentful.
translations.idiomatic: if management is inept, clerks grow corrupt and the people resentful.

sentences.zh: 又差發徭役，多不存意。

translations.literal: Again in assigning corvée labor, many give no thought to fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In assigning corvée labor, too, many give no thought to fairness.

sentences.zh: 致令貧弱者或重徭而遠戍，富強者或輕使而近防。

translations.idiomatic: The poor may bear heavy corvée and serve on distant frontiers, while the rich receive light duty and guard nearby.

sentences.zh: 守令用懷如此，不存恤民之心，皆王政之罪人也。

translations.literal: Magistrates whose intent is like this, not keeping care for the people in mind, are all criminals against the royal government.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who think this way, with no care for the people, are criminals against royal government.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚重之，常置諸座右。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai greatly valued it and always kept it at his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai valued it greatly and always kept it at his side.

sentences.zh: 又令百司習誦之。

translations.literal: He also ordered the hundred offices to study and recite it.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered every office to study and recite it.

sentences.zh: 其牧守令長，非通六條及計帳者，不得居官。

translations.literal: Regional governors, prefects, and magistrates who did not thoroughly know the Six Ordinances and account books could not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: No governor, prefect, or magistrate who had not mastered the Six Ordinances and the account books could hold office.

sentences.zh: 自有晉之季，文章競為浮華，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: From the late Jin onward, writing competed in being ornate and flowery, and this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Jin onward, writing grew ever more ornate until florid style became the norm.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲革其弊，因魏帝祭廟，羣臣畢至，乃命綽為大誥，奏行之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wished to reform this abuse; when the Wei emperor sacrificed at the ancestral temple and all the ministers had assembled, he ordered Su Chuo to compose a Great Announcement and memorialize it for promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wished to reform the abuse. When the Wei emperor sacrificed at the ancestral temple and all the ministers were present, he had Su Chuo compose a Great Announcement and memorialized it for promulgation.

sentences.zh: 惟中興十有一年，仲夏，庶邦百辟，咸會於王庭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Restoration, in midsummer, the myriad states and hundred ministers all assembled at the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Restoration, in midsummer, the myriad states and all ministers assembled at the royal court.

sentences.zh: 柱國泰洎羣公列將，罔不來朝。

translations.literal: The Pillar of State and all the grandees and ranking generals, none failed to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Pillar of State and all the grandees and ranking generals came to court without exception.

sentences.zh: 時乃大稽百憲，敷於庶邦，用綏我王度。

translations.literal: Then a great review of the hundred laws was made, proclaimed to the myriad states, to stabilize our royal institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Then the hundred laws were reviewed in full, proclaimed to the myriad states, and royal order was secured.

sentences.zh: 皇帝曰：「昔堯命羲和，允厘百工。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In antiquity Yao charged Xi and He, truly to regulate the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "In antiquity Yao charged Xi and He to regulate the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 舜命九官，庶績咸熙。

translations.literal: Shun appointed the Nine Ministers, and all achievements were glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Shun appointed the Nine Ministers, and every task flourished.

sentences.zh: 武丁命說，克號高宗。

translations.literal: Wu Ding charged Yue, and worthily was styled High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ding charged Yue, and worthily earned the title High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 時惟休哉，朕其欽若。

translations.literal: The time was truly splendid—I shall reverently follow their example.
translations.idiomatic: Those were glorious ages; I shall reverently follow their example.
