translations.literal: To you who hold office, all having come to our Grand Progenitor's court, I will grandly charge you with your posts."
translations.idiomatic: You who hold office, having all come to our Grand Progenitor's court—I will grandly charge you with your posts."

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳，皇帝朝格於太廟，凡厥具僚，罔不在位。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month, the Emperor offered morning rites at the Grand Temple; all his officers, none were not in place.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month the Emperor offered morning rites at the Grand Temple; every officer was in his place.

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「咨我元輔、羣公、列將、百辟、卿士、庶尹、禦事，朕惟寅敷祖宗之靈命，稽于先王之典訓，以大誥于爾在位。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Consult, my chief minister, grandees, ranking generals, hundred ministers, ministers, officials, and officers—I reverently spread forth the spiritual mandate of the ancestors, examine the canonical instructions of the former kings, and with a Great Announcement address you who hold office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Chief minister, grandees, ranking generals, hundred ministers, ministers, officials, and officers—I reverently carry out the spiritual mandate of the ancestors, consult the canonical instructions of the former kings, and address you who hold office with this Great Announcement.

sentences.zh: 昔我太祖神皇，肇膺明命，以創我皇基。

translations.literal: In antiquity our Grand Progenitor the Divine Emperor first received the bright mandate and founded our royal foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity our Grand Progenitor the Divine Emperor first received the bright mandate and founded our royal house.

sentences.zh: 烈祖景宗，廓開四表，底定武功。

translations.literal: Our resolute ancestor the Illustrious Emperor opened the four quarters and settled martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Our resolute ancestor the Illustrious Emperor opened the four quarters and settled the realm by force of arms.

sentences.zh: 暨乎文祖，誕敷文德，龔惟武考，不霣其舊。

translations.literal: Down to the Literary Ancestor, who broadly spread civil virtue, and our martial forebear, who did not let the old order fall.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the Literary Ancestor, who spread civil virtue abroad, and our martial forebear, who did not let the old order fall.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，陵夷之弊，用興大難於彼東丘，則我黎人，咸墜塗炭。

translations.literal: From that time onward, decline and corruption arose, and great calamity was raised at that eastern mound; then our black-haired people all fell into fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: After that decline set in, great disaster arose in the east, and our people fell into fire and water.

sentences.zh: 惟臺一人，纘戎下武，夙夜祗畏，若涉大川，罔識攸濟。

translations.literal: I alone, continuing the martial legacy and following the former kings, day and night held reverent awe, as if crossing a great river, not knowing how to reach the other shore.
translations.idiomatic: I alone, inheriting the martial legacy of the former kings, am reverently on guard day and night, as one crossing a great river without knowing how to reach the farther shore.

sentences.zh: 是用稽於帝典，揆于王廷，拯我民瘼。

translations.literal: Therefore I examine the canon of the emperors and measure affairs at the royal court, to rescue our people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I consult the canon of the emperors and weigh affairs at court to rescue the people from distress.

sentences.zh: 惟彼哲王，示我彝訓，曰天生蒸民，罔克自乂，上帝降鑒叡聖，植元後以乂之。

translations.literal: That wise king showed us the constant instruction, saying: Heaven gave birth to the multitude; they cannot govern themselves. Heaven sent down a discerning and sage ruler and set up the chief to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: That wise king showed us the constant instruction: Heaven gave birth to the multitude, but they cannot govern themselves; Heaven sent down a discerning sage and set up a chief to govern them.

sentences.zh: 惟時元後弗克獨乂，博求明德，命百辟羣吏以佐之。

translations.literal: At that time the chief could not govern alone; he broadly sought the bright and virtuous and charged the hundred ministers and all officials to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief could not govern alone; he sought the bright and virtuous and charged the hundred ministers and all officials to assist him.

sentences.zh: 肆天之命辟，辟之命官，惟以恤民，弗惟逸念。

translations.literal: Thus Heaven's mandate reaches the chief, and the chief's mandate reaches the officers—only to care for the people, not to think of ease alone.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate reaches the chief, and the chief's mandate reaches the officers—all to care for the people, not to seek ease alone.

sentences.zh: 辟惟元首，庶黎惟趾，股肱惟弼。

translations.literal: The chief is the head, the multitude are the feet, and the ministers are the supporting limbs.
translations.idiomatic: The chief is the head, the people are the feet, and the ministers are the supporting limbs.

sentences.zh: 上下一體，各勤攸司，茲用克臻於皇極。

translations.literal: Above and below are one body; each diligently performs his charge—thus one can reach the supreme standard.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below form one body; each diligently performs his charge—and so the supreme standard can be reached.

sentences.zh: 故其彝訓曰：「后克艱厥後，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂。

translations.literal: Therefore its constant instruction says: "The ruler who can be stern with himself, the minister who can be stern with himself—then government is well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the constant instruction says: "When the ruler is stern with himself and the minister is stern with himself, government is well ordered.

sentences.zh: 」今台一人，膺天之嘏，旣陟元后。

translations.literal: " Now I alone, receiving Heaven's blessing, have ascended to be chief.
translations.idiomatic: " Now I alone, receiving Heaven's blessing, have ascended to be chief.

sentences.zh: 股肱百辟又服我國家之命，罔不咸守厥職。

translations.literal: The supporting limbs, the hundred ministers, again obey our state's mandate; none fail to keep their posts.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers, the hundred officers, again obey our state's mandate; none fail to keep your posts.

sentences.zh: 嗟夫，後弗艱厥後，臣弗艱厥臣，於政何弗斁，嗚呼艱哉！

translations.literal: Alas! If the ruler is not stern with himself and the minister is not stern with himself, how can government not fail? Ah, how hard it is!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! If ruler and minister are not stern with themselves, how can government not fail? Ah, how hard it is!

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Pillar of State, the realm has not yet been settled, for nearly two reign periods.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Pillar of State, the realm has not yet been settled, for nearly two reign periods.

sentences.zh: 天未絕我太祖列祖之命，用錫我以元輔。

translations.literal: Heaven has not cut off the mandate of our Grand Progenitor and successive ancestors, and has granted me a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has not cut off the mandate of our Grand Progenitor and successive ancestors, and has granted me a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 國家將墜，公惟棟樑。

translations.literal: The state was about to collapse—you alone were its pillar.
translations.idiomatic: The state was about to collapse—you alone were its pillar.

sentences.zh: 皇之弗極，公作相。

translations.literal: The throne was not yet established—you served as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was not yet established—you served as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 百揆諐度，公惟大錄。

translations.literal: The hundred offices were in disorder—you alone were the great recorder.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices were in disorder—you alone were the great recorder.

sentences.zh: 公其允文允武，克明克乂，迪七德，敷九功，龕暴除亂，下綏我蒼生，旁施於九土。

translations.literal: You have been both literary and martial, both discerning and governing, advancing the seven virtues and spreading the nine achievements, pacifying violence and removing disorder, soothing our black-haired people below and extending grace to the nine regions.
translations.idiomatic: You have been both literary and martial, both discerning and governing, advancing the seven virtues and spreading the nine achievements, pacifying violence and removing disorder, soothing our people below and extending grace to the nine regions.

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「羣公、太宰、太尉、司徒、司空。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Grandees, Grand Steward, Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Grandees, Grand Steward, Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 惟公作朕鼎足，以弼乎朕躬。

translations.literal: You alone are my tripod legs, to assist my person.
translations.idiomatic: You are the three legs of my tripod, supporting my person.

sentences.zh: 宰惟天官，克諧六職。

translations.literal: The Steward is the officer of Heaven, harmonizing the six duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Steward is Heaven's officer, harmonizing the six duties.

sentences.zh: 尉惟司武，武在止戈。

translations.literal: The Commandant is the officer of war; the aim of war is to stop warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant is the officer of war; the aim of war is to stop warfare.

sentences.zh: 徒惟司眾，敬敷五教。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education is the officer of the multitude, reverently spreading the five teachings.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education is the officer of the multitude, reverently spreading the five teachings.

sentences.zh: 空惟司土，利用厚生。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works is the officer of earth, using resources to enrich life.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works is the officer of earth, using resources to enrich life.

sentences.zh: 惟時三事，若三階之在天；

translations.literal: At this time the Three Dignities are like the Three Steps in heaven;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Three Dignities are like the Three Steps in heaven;

sentences.zh: 惟茲四輔，若四時之成歲。

translations.literal: And these Four Supports are like the four seasons completing the year.
translations.idiomatic: And these Four Supports are like the four seasons completing the year.

translations.idiomatic: May you carry out Heaven's work in its place."

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Commanders-in-chief, you shall soar like hawks and be My talons and fangs; against bandits, thieves, traitors, and wicked men, against barbarians who vex China—you go forth to punish; soothe with kindness, oversee with authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Commanders-in-chief, you shall soar like hawks and be My talons and fangs; against bandits, thieves, traitors, and wicked men, against barbarians who vex China—you go forth to punish; soothe with kindness, oversee with authority.

translations.literal: Aim at punishment so that punishment may cease; let all regions be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Aim at punishment so that punishment may cease; let all regions be at peace.

translations.literal: Make it so that within the eight directions none disobey Our command—that will be your merit.
translations.idiomatic: Make it so that within the eight directions none disobey Our command—that will be your merit.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Princes of the many domains, you guard the land and are fathers and mothers to the people.

sentences.zh: 民惟不勝其饑，故先王重農；

translations.literal: The people cannot prevail against hunger, so the former kings prized agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot prevail against hunger, so the former kings prized agriculture;

translations.idiomatic: They cannot prevail against cold, so the former kings valued women's work.

translations.literal: If the people do not follow filial piety and kindness, then ties of kin grow thin;
translations.idiomatic: If the people do not follow filial piety and kindness, then ties of kin grow thin;

translations.literal: If they are not earnest in rites and yielding, then strife and seizure arise.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not earnest in rites and yielding, then strife and seizure arise.

translations.literal: These six things are truly the root of teaching.
translations.idiomatic: These six things are truly the root of teaching.

translations.idiomatic: Balance them with rites: neither hard nor soft, and measure to the utmost of the Way."

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Ministers, lesser directors, and all who handle affairs—the king examines by the year, ministers by the month, directors by the day, handlers by the hour.

translations.literal: Year, month, day, and hour—do not alter their measures; all statutes will be upheld, and many achievements will consolidate.

translations.idiomatic: You royal officers blend and balance the myriad states, as heaven has the Dipper—you measure out primal energy, temper yin and yang, never lose harmony, and the people will forever rely on you;

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In the Way of heaven and earth, there is one yin and one yang;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "In the Way of heaven and earth, there is one yin and one yang;

translations.literal: In the change of rites and custom, one refinement and one plainness.
translations.idiomatic: In the change of rites and custom, one refinement and one plainness.

translations.literal: From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors down to the present, change is not merely change—it is to remedy abuses; succession is not merely succession—it is what can endure.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors down to the present, change is not merely change—it is to remedy abuses; succession is not merely succession—it is what can endure.

translations.literal: Our Wei alone inherits the late drift of Zhou, meets the lingering abuses of Qin and Han, takes up the florid falsehoods of Wei and Jin; five ages of thin custom have still not been reformed—can we bring calm to custom and raise transformation to that end?
translations.idiomatic: Our Wei alone inherits the late drift of Zhou, meets the lingering abuses of Qin and Han, takes up the florid falsehoods of Wei and Jin; five ages of thin custom have still not been reformed—can we bring calm to custom and raise transformation to that end?

translations.idiomatic: I charge you who hold office: join with My heart, make virtue solid and be trustworthy, and make this hardship your sole task.

translations.literal: Cast off ornament, embrace substance; turn from falsehood, honor sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Cast off ornament, embrace substance; turn from falsehood, honor sincerity.

translations.literal: Do not err, do not forget—unite with the eternal canons of the Three Dynasties, return to moral virtue and humaneness and righteousness, and thereby protect the great mandate of our ancestors.

translations.literal: Bear heaven's favor, be able to pacify our myriad regions, and forever bring peace to our people.

translations.literal: " The kings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors all followed this Way and thereby reached the point where punishments were set aside.
translations.idiomatic: " The kings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors all followed this Way and thereby reached the point where punishments were set aside.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，歷千載而未聞。

translations.literal: Since that age, a thousand years have passed and it has not been heard of again.
translations.idiomatic: Since that age, a thousand years have passed and it has not been heard of again.

sentences.zh: 惟帝念功，將反叔世，逖致於雍。

translations.literal: Only the Emperor, mindful of merit, will turn back the decadent age and bring far peace.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Emperor, mindful of merit, will turn back the decadent age and bring far peace.

sentences.zh: 庸錫降丕命於我羣臣。

translations.literal: Hence he has granted his great mandate to us ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hence he has granted his great mandate to us ministers.

sentences.zh: 博哉王言，非言之難，行之實難。

translations.literal: How broad the king's words! It is not speech that is hard—it is action that is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: How broad the king's words! It is not speech that is hard—it is action that is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 罔不有初，鮮克有終。

translations.literal: Nothing lacks a beginning; few reach the end.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing lacks a beginning; few reach the end.

sentences.zh: 《商書》曰：『終始惟一，德乃日新。

translations.literal: The Book of Shang says: "From beginning to end be one, and virtue daily renews.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Shang says: "From beginning to end be one, and virtue daily renews.

sentences.zh: 』惟帝敬厥始，慎厥終，以躋日新之德，則我羣臣，敢不夙夜對揚休哉。

translations.literal: " If the Emperor reveres the beginning and is careful at the end, ascending to daily-renewing virtue, then we ministers—how dare we not from early till late respond and spread this excellence!
translations.idiomatic: " If the Emperor reveres the beginning and is careful at the end, ascending to daily-renewing virtue, then we ministers—how dare we not from early till late respond and spread this excellence!

sentences.zh: 惟茲大誼，未光於四表，以邁種德，俾九域幽遐，咸昭奉元後之明訓，率遷於道，永膺無疆之休。」

translations.literal: Only let this great principle shine to the four quarters; planting virtue far and wide, make the nine regions, however remote, all clearly follow the supreme ruler's bright instruction, one and all move toward the Way, and forever receive boundless blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Only let this great principle shine to the four quarters; planting virtue far and wide, make the nine regions, however remote, all clearly follow the supreme ruler's bright instruction, one and all move toward the Way, and forever receive boundless blessing."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「欽哉。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Take heed."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Take heed."

sentences.zh: 自是之後，文筆皆依此體。

translations.literal: From this time onward, all official writing followed this style.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, all official writing followed this style.

sentences.zh: 綽性儉素，不治產業，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Su Chuo by nature was frugal and plain, did not manage property, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo was frugal and plain by nature, did not manage property, and his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 以海內未平，常以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Because the realm within the seas was not yet settled, he constantly took all under Heaven as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was not yet settled, he constantly took all under Heaven as his own charge.

sentences.zh: 博求賢俊，共弘治道，凡所薦達，皆至大官。

translations.literal: He widely sought worthy and outstanding men to together enlarge the Way of governance; all he recommended and promoted reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: He widely sought worthy men to enlarge the Way of governance together; every man he recommended rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦推心委任，而無間言。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also gave him his full trust and delegated authority, and there was never a word of dissension between them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also gave him his full trust and delegated authority, and there was never a word of dissension between them.

sentences.zh: 太祖或出遊，常預署空紙以授綽，若須有處分，則隨事施行，及還，啟之而已。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor went touring, he would often pre-sign blank sheets and give them to Su Chuo; if any decision was needed, Su Chuo would act according to the matter, and when Grand Progenitor returned he need only be informed—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor went touring, he would often pre-sign blank sheets and give them to Su Chuo; if any decision was needed, Su Chuo would act on the spot, and when Grand Progenitor returned he need only be informed—that was all.

sentences.zh: 綽嘗謂治國之道，當愛民如慈父，訓民如嚴師。

translations.literal: Su Chuo once said that the Way of governing a state is to love the people as a kindly father loves them and to instruct the people as a strict teacher instructs them.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo once said that the Way of governing a state is to love the people as a kindly father and instruct them as a strict teacher.

sentences.zh: 每與公卿議論，自晝達夜，事無巨細，若指諸掌。

translations.literal: Whenever he debated with the chief ministers, it ran from day into night; matters great and small seemed laid out on the palm of his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he debated with the chief ministers, it ran from day into night; matters great and small seemed laid out on the palm of his hand.

sentences.zh: 積思勞倦，遂成氣疾。

translations.literal: Accumulated thought and toil brought weariness, and he thereupon developed a qi disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated thought and toil brought weariness, and he thereupon developed a qi disorder.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒于位，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died in office, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太祖痛惜之，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor grieved and cherished his memory; his sorrow moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor grieved and cherished his memory; his sorrow moved those around him.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，乃謂公卿等曰：「蘇尚書平生謙退，敦尚儉約。

translations.literal: When the burial was at hand, he said to the chief ministers: "Master of Writing Su in his lifetime was humble and retiring, and honored thrift and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was at hand, he said to the chief ministers: "Master of Writing Su in his lifetime was humble and retiring, and honored thrift and restraint.

sentences.zh: 吾欲全其素志，便恐悠悠之徒，有所未達；

translations.literal: I wish to honor his lifelong intent, but fear that idle gossips may not understand;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to honor his lifelong intent, but fear that idle gossips may not understand;

sentences.zh: 如其厚加贈諡，又乖宿昔相知之道。

translations.literal: Yet if I richly bestow posthumous honors and title, that too would go against the bond of long friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I richly bestow posthumous honors and title, that too would go against the bond of long friendship.

sentences.zh: 進退惟穀，孤有疑焉。

translations.literal: Advancing or holding back—I alone am undecided."
translations.idiomatic: Advancing or holding back—I alone am undecided."

sentences.zh: 」尚書令史麻瑤越次而進曰：「昔晏子，齊之賢大夫，一狐裘三十年。

translations.literal: Secretariat section chief Ma Yao overstepping rank advanced and said: "In olden days Yanzi, Qi state's worthy grandee, wore one fox-fur coat for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat section chief Ma Yao overstepping rank advanced and said: "In olden days Yanzi, Qi state's worthy grandee, wore one fox-fur coat for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，遺車一乘。

translations.literal: When he died, he left a single cart.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he left a single cart.

sentences.zh: 齊侯不奪其志。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Qi did not override his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Qi did not override his intent.

sentences.zh: 綽旣操履清白，謙挹自居，愚謂宜從儉約，以彰其美。

translations.literal: Su Chuo's conduct was pure and white, and he lived in humility and restraint—I hold that he should be buried with thrift to display his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo's conduct was pure and white, and he lived in humility and restraint—I hold that he should be buried with thrift to display his virtue."

sentences.zh: 」太祖稱善，因薦瑤於朝廷。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor praised this, and on that account recommended Ma Yao to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor praised this, and on that account recommended Ma Yao to the court.

sentences.zh: 及綽歸葬武功，唯載以布車一乘。

translations.literal: When Su Chuo was returned for burial at Wugong, he was carried on a single cloth-covered cart.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Chuo was returned for burial at Wugong, he was carried on a single cloth-covered cart.

sentences.zh: 太祖與羣公，皆步送出同州郭門外。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor with all the lords walked on foot to see him off outside Tong Province's outer gate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor with all the lords walked on foot to see him off outside Tong Province's outer gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖親于車後酹酒而言曰：「尚書平生為事，妻子兄弟不知者，吾皆知之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor personally poured libation behind the carriage and said: "In his lifetime the Master of Writing did things his wife, children, and brothers did not know of—but I knew them all.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor personally poured libation behind the carriage and said: "In his lifetime the Master of Writing did things his wife, children, and brothers did not know of—but I knew them all.

sentences.zh: 惟爾知吾心，吾知爾意。

translations.literal: Only you know my heart, and I know your intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only you know my heart, and I know your intent.

sentences.zh: 方欲共定天下，不幸遂舍我去，奈何！

translations.literal: We were just about to settle all under Heaven together, when unfortunately he left me—what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: We were just about to settle all under Heaven together, when unfortunately he left me—what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 」因舉聲慟哭，不覺失卮於手。

translations.literal: He then raised his voice and wept bitterly, unaware that he had dropped the cup from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his voice and wept bitterly, unaware that he had dropped the cup from his hand.

sentences.zh: 至葬日，又遣使祭乙太牢，太祖自為其文。

translations.literal: On the burial day he again sent an envoy to sacrifice a second-grade offering of ox, sheep, and pig, and Grand Progenitor wrote the sacrificial text himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day he again sent an envoy to sacrifice a second-grade offering of ox, sheep, and pig, and Grand Progenitor wrote the sacrificial text himself.

sentences.zh: 綽乂著《佛性論》、《七經論》，並行於世。

translations.literal: Su Chuo also wrote On the Buddha Nature and On the Seven Classics, both of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo also wrote On the Buddha Nature and On the Seven Classics, both of which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 明帝二年，以綽配享太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ming, Su Chuo was given paired sacrifice in Grand Progenitor's ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming, Su Chuo was given paired sacrifice in Grand Progenitor's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 子威嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 威少有父風，襲爵美陽伯。

translations.literal: Wei from youth had his father's bearing; he inherited the title Baron of Meiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei from youth had his father's bearing; he inherited the title Baron of Meiyang.

sentences.zh: 娶晉公護女新興公主，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵懷道縣公。

translations.literal: He married Princess Xinxing, daughter of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Huaidao county.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Xinxing, daughter of Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Huaidao county.

sentences.zh: 建德初，稍遷御伯下大夫。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiande he was gradually promoted to Under Master of the Imperial Guard, lower grand master.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiande he was gradually promoted to Under Master of the Imperial Guard, lower grand master.

sentences.zh: 大象末，開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, opening-office equal-in-protocol grand general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang he was made opening-office equal-in-protocol grand general.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，以綽著名前代，乃下詔曰：「昔漢高欽無忌之義，魏武挹子幹之風，前代名賢，後王斯重。

translations.literal: At the start of Sui's Kaihuang era, because Su Chuo had been famous in the former age, an edict was issued: "In olden days Emperor Gao of Han admired the righteousness of Wang Ling; Emperor Wu of Wei drew upon the spirit of Cao Zigan—former ages' eminent worthies were honored by later kings.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Sui's Kaihuang era, because Su Chuo had been famous in the former age, an edict was issued: "In olden days Emperor Gao of Han admired the righteousness of Wang Ling; Emperor Wu of Wei drew upon the spirit of Cao Zigan—former ages' eminent worthies were honored by later kings.

sentences.zh: 魏故度支尚書、美陽伯蘇綽，文雅政事，遺跡可稱。

translations.literal: Former Wei Director of Revenue, Baron of Meiyang Su Chuo—in literary elegance and administration his traces are worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Former Wei Director of Revenue, Baron of Meiyang Su Chuo—in literary elegance and administration his traces are worth praise.

sentences.zh: 展力前王，垂聲著績。

translations.literal: He deployed his strength for the former king and left lasting fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed his strength for the former king and left lasting fame and achievement.

sentences.zh: 宜開土宇，用旌善人。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open territory and reward the good man."
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to open territory and reward the good man."

sentences.zh: 」於是追封邳國公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su Chuo was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Pi state, fief two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Su Chuo was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Pi state, fief two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 綽弟椿，字令欽。

translations.literal: Su Chuo's younger brother Chun, styled Lingqin.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo's younger brother Chun, styled Lingqin.

sentences.zh: 性廉慎，沉勇有決斷。

translations.literal: By nature he was honest and cautious, deep and brave with decisive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was honest and cautious, deep and brave with decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 正光中，關右賊亂，椿應募討之，授蕩寇將軍。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang, when bandits rose in the west of the Passes, Chun answered the call to campaign against them and was appointed Bandit-Suppressing General.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang, when bandits rose in the west of the Passes, Chun answered the call to campaign against them and was appointed Bandit-Suppressing General.

sentences.zh: 累功

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit

translations.literal: (Enfeoffed)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: enfeoffed]

sentences.zh: 遷奉朝請、厲威將軍、中散大夫，賜爵美陽子，加都督、持節、平西將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant at Court, Fierce-Power General, and Grand Master in Attendance, enfeoffed Baron of Meiyang, and additionally made area commander, bearing the staff, Pacifying-West General, and Grand Master for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant at Court, Fierce-Power General, and Grand Master in Attendance, enfeoffed Baron of Meiyang, and additionally made area commander, bearing the staff, Pacifying-West General, and Grand Master for All Purposes.

sentences.zh: 大統初，拜鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，賜姓賀蘭氏。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong, he was appointed Pacifying-East General and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Tether, and granted the surname Helan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong, he was appointed Pacifying-East General and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Tether, and granted the surname Helan.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為武都郡守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as administrator of Wudu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went out as administrator of Wudu commandery.

sentences.zh: 改授西夏州長史，除帥都督，行弘農郡事。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as chief administrator of Western Xia Province, appointed campaign-area commander, and acted in the affairs of Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as chief administrator of Western Xia Province, appointed campaign-area commander, and acted in the affairs of Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 椿當官強濟，特為太祖所知。

translations.literal: Chun in office was forceful and efficient, and was especially known to Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Chun in office was forceful and efficient, and was especially known to Grand Progenitor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，置當州鄉帥，自非鄉望允當眾心，不得預焉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, township commanders were established in the province; unless one's local standing matched the people's hearts, one could not be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, township commanders were established in the province; unless one's local standing matched the people's hearts, one could not be appointed.

sentences.zh: 乃令驛追椿領鄉兵。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor therefore sent a courier post-haste to summon Chun to lead township troops.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor therefore sent a courier post-haste to summon Chun to lead township troops.

sentences.zh: 其年，破槃頭氐有功，除散騎常侍，加大都督。

translations.literal: That year, for merit in defeating the Pantou Di, he was appointed Regular Attendant at the Royal Court and given the additional title of great area commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for merit in defeating the Pantou Di, he was appointed Regular Attendant at the Royal Court and given the additional title of great area commander.

sentences.zh: 十六年，征隨郡，軍還，除武功郡守。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he campaigned against Suizhou commandery; when the army returned he was appointed administrator of Wugong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he campaigned against Suizhou commandery; when the army returned he was appointed administrator of Wugong commandery.

sentences.zh: 旣為本邑，以清儉自居，小大之政，必盡忠恕。

translations.literal: Since this was his native district, he maintained himself in purity and thrift; in small and great affairs of government he always exerted loyalty and forbearance fully.
translations.idiomatic: Since this was his native district, he maintained himself in purity and thrift; in small and great affairs of government he always exerted loyalty and forbearance fully.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional commission bearing the staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional commission bearing the staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and advanced in enfeoffment to marquis.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, he was promoted to Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, opening-office equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and great area commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng, he was promoted to Grand General of Rapid Cavalry, opening-office equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, and great area commander.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 子植嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《書》云：「惟後非賢弗乂，惟賢非後罔食」。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Book (Documents) says: "Only rulers who are not worthy cannot govern; only the worthy who are not rulers cannot eat."
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The Documents say: "If the sovereign is not worthy, he cannot govern; if the worthy man is not sovereign, he cannot find sustenance."

sentences.zh: 是以知人則哲，有國之所先；

translations.literal: Therefore knowing men makes one wise; it is the first priority for one who holds a state;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to know men is wisdom, and for one who holds a state it comes first;

sentences.zh: 用之則行，為下之常道。

translations.literal: employing them then [policy] proceeds; it is the constant way for subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: and to employ them is to put policy into action—the constant duty of ministers.

sentences.zh: 若乃庖廚、胥靡、種德、微管之臣，罕聞於世；

translations.literal: As for ministers like cooks, convict laborers, planters of virtue, and Guan Zhong in obscurity, they are rarely heard of in the world;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yiyin the cook, Fuyue the prisoner, Gao Yao who "advanced in planting virtue," and Guan Zhong in humble obscurity are rarely celebrated in their own time;

sentences.zh: 黜魯、逐荊、抱關、執戟之士，無乏於時。

translations.literal: Those demoted from Lu, expelled in Jing, gatekeepers, and halberd-bearers—never lacking in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men demoted from Lu, banished in Chu, gatekeepers, and halberd-bearers were never wanting in any age.

sentences.zh: 斯固《典慕》所以昭則，《風雅》所以興刺也。

translations.literal: This is precisely why the "Dian Mo" displays norms and the "Feng Ya" raises satire.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Documents set forth standards and the Odes stir rebuke.

sentences.zh: 誠能監前事之得喪，勞虛己於吐握，其知賢也必用，其授爵也勿疑，則舜禹湯武之德可連衡矣，稷契伊呂之流可比肩矣。

translations.literal: If one can truly observe the gain and loss of prior affairs, exhaust oneself in emptying the self at spitting-and-gripping [receiving talents], when knowing the worthy must employ them, when granting titles must not doubt—then the virtue of Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wu can be joined in measure, and men like Ji, Xie, Yi, and Lü can be matched shoulder to shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers could truly weigh past success and failure, humble themselves as Duke of Zhou did when he "spit out his food and released his hair grip" to receive men, employ the worthy without fail, and grant office without hesitation, then the virtue of Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wu would stand in one line and men like Hou Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, and Lü Shang could walk shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 太祖提劍而起，百度草創。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor raised sword and rose; the hundred offices were newly established.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai drew sword and rose to power when every institution had still to be created.

sentences.zh: 施約法之制於競逐之辰，脩治定之禮於鼎峙之日。

translations.literal: He implemented simplified-law institutions in the season of competitive pursuit, cultivated order-and-stability rites in the days of tripod standoff.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed austere law amid fierce rivalry and built stable rites while rival states still stood like the legs of a tripod.

sentences.zh: 終能斲雕為朴，變奢從儉，風化旣被，而下肅上尊；

translations.literal: In the end he was able to carve ornament into plainness, change luxury to follow frugality; when custom and transformation had been spread, below was reverent and above was honored;
translations.idiomatic: In the end he stripped ornament back to plainness and turned luxury toward frugality; once custom had taken hold, inferiors were reverent and superiors were honored;

sentences.zh: 疆埸屢擾，而內親外附。

translations.literal: The borderlands were repeatedly disturbed, yet within there was closeness and without there was attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Though the frontiers were repeatedly disturbed, within the realm kinship held firm and outside powers drew near in alliance.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋蘇令綽之力也。

translations.literal: This was surely the power of Su Lingzuo.
translations.idiomatic: That was largely the work of Su Lingzuo (Su Chuo).

sentences.zh: 名冠當時，慶流後嗣，宜哉。

translations.literal: Fame topped the age, blessing flowed to later descendants—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: First in fame in his own day, a blessing to his descendants—entirely as it should be.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
